reconcile.note: Jamieson, Fausset & Brown limit Isaiah's filthy-rags verdict to the unregenerate's own righteousness, distinct from the Spirit-wrought goodness Luke ascribes to Joseph.

discrepancy.emptyNote: Steve Wells's Skeptic's Annotated Bible treats Isaiah's filthy-rags verdict on human righteousness as flatly inconsistent with Luke calling Joseph a good and righteous man.

sides.snippet: For we are all become as one who is unclean, and all our righteousness are as a polluted garment: and we all do fade as a leaf; and our iniquities, like the wind, take us away.
sides.verseText: For we are all become as one who is unclean, and all our righteousness are as a polluted garment: and we all do fade as a leaf; and our iniquities, like the wind, take us away.

sides.snippet: Behold, a man named Joseph, who was a member of the council, a good and righteous man
sides.verseText: Behold, a man named Joseph, who was a member of the council, a good and righteous man
